subject: FablePay p95 surge: shortlist product asks, SRE runbook, and customer-ready note
messages:
From: Elaine Huang <elaine@fablepay.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-09T08:12:00-07:00
Subject: p95 latency spike observed on production (us-west)

Hi Jasmine —

We started seeing a p95 latency spike from ~07:55 PDT that affected token-generation endpoints for our checkout flow. Error rates are low, but median is fine and tail is spiking (p95 ~1.8s -> 4.2s). This started after your 07:30 rollout (we're pinned to model v2.3.1). Can you confirm if Redwood is seeing this from your side and what immediate mitigation looks like?

Attached are traces and a short sample of request IDs. We have a big promo running and this is impacting conversions.

—Elaine
Elaine Huang
Head of Engineering, FablePay
[attachment: fablepay_traces_080926.txt]

From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine@redwood.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ryan Smith <ryan.smith@fablepay.com>
Date: 2026-08-09T08:25:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: p95 latency spike observed on production (us-west)

Forwarding Elaine's note — FablePay is seeing a pronounced p95 jump in us-west starting ~07:55 after our rollout. Ryan is copied.

Immediate asks:
- Can SRE confirm if this correlates with the 07:30 model roll? (Soojin)
- Product: short list of possible mitigations to reduce tail (Karthik) — quantization toggle, smaller kv-cache size, routing to older model?
- CS/AM (Marissa/Ben): prepare a short, non-technical customer note with ETA for a fix and a recommended workaround.

I will coordinate the customer comms once we have a clear mitigation path. Attaching the traces Elaine sent.

Thanks —
Jasmine
Customer Reliability Manager, Redwood Inference

From: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.ai>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ryan Smith <ryan.smith@fablepay.com>
Date: 2026-08-09T08:47:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: p95 latency spike observed on production (us-west)

Quick triage update:
- Confirmed: spike aligns with the 07:30 deployment of model v2.3.1 in us-west for FablePay's routing policy (they were pinned but auto-rolled under compatible-variants policy).
- Error rates stayed low; signs point to KV-cache warming + a slightly changed attention kernel path in v2.3.1 that increases tail on long-seq requests.
- Immediate mitigation I can apply now (low-risk): roll FablePay back to v2.3.0 on their dedicated pool (takes ~4–6 min to drain gracefully) OR apply a temporary routing rule to send 30% of traffic to v2.3.0 as a canary.

Artifacts requested from FablePay (already included): request-IDs, sample prompts. I'll also pull internal runtime metrics (KV hit/miss, scheduling delays) and upload to the shared drive link.

I'll start the partial rollback if we agree — prefer a controlled 30% canary first so we can compare real-time metrics before full rollback.

Soojin
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference
[attachment: perf_dump_2026-08-09.zip (120MB)]

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ryan Smith <ryan.smith@fablepay.com>
Date: 2026-08-09T09:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: p95 latency spike observed on production (us-west)

Notes from product side — short actionable items:
1) Canary routing (30%) to v2.3.0: good first step. If p95 drops back for canary, proceed to full rollback.
2) Runtime knob: temporarily disable the new attention kernel micro-optimizations that appear to regress long-sequence tails (low-risk flag, no model change). We can toggle via config and monitor impact within 2–3 min.
3) KV-cache tune: reduce per-request kv_cache_prefetch to force warmer cache behavior for this workload (minor latency trade-off for tail stability).

If we do a rollback, add a postmortem action: identify sequence-length distribution that triggered the kernel path and consider a targeted kernel-selection rule.

I'll prepare the change and a short changelog entry. Jasmine — can you confirm customer messaging cadence?

Karthik
Director, Product — Serving Runtime

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
Bcc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-09T09:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: p95 latency spike observed on production (us-west)

Customer note (draft) — short, clear, non-technical:
Hi Elaine / Ryan —

Thank you for flagging this. We’re seeing a tail latency spike affecting some checkout requests in us-west following a routine deployment this morning. We have a mitigation plan underway and expect to restore normal p95 within 30–45 minutes.

What we’re doing now:
- Running a targeted canary to validate behavior on previous model (30% traffic)
- If validated, we will complete a full rollback — no action needed from your side

We will follow up with a short summary once resolved and a next-step note describing what caused the issue and what we’ll change to avoid it.

Is it OK to send this now? I kept the language neutral and time-bounded.

—Marissa
Customer Success Manager

From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine@redwood.ai>
To: Elaine Huang <elaine@fablepay.com>, Ryan Smith <ryan.smith@fablepay.com>
Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-10T15:42:00-07:00
Subject: Update: FablePay p95 tail spike — resolution and next steps

Elaine / Ryan —

Thanks for your patience. Quick update and final state: 

Timeline / actions taken:
- 08:47 — Investigated and confirmed correlation with v2.3.1 rollout.
- 08:50–09:05 — Deployed 30% canary to v2.3.0; observed p95 drop back to baseline for canary traffic.
- 09:08 — Completed full rollback to v2.3.0 for FablePay's dedicated pool (graceful drain).
- 09:20 — Monitored metrics: p95 stabilized to baseline ~1.9s within 20 minutes.

Root cause (short): an attention-kernel selection path in v2.3.1 that increases tail for long-sequence checkout prompts combined with KV-cache warmup behavior for this workload.

Next steps (internal):
- Product (Karthik): introduce targeted kernel-selection rule and include sequence-length guardrail in the next sprint.
- SRE (Soojin): add a runbook step to automatically trigger 30% canary routing when tail deviation > 30% post-rollout for pinned customers.
- CS (Marissa): send the customer postmortem and roadmap ask.

Attached: perf_dump_2026-08-09.zip and a short draft postmortem. Link to logs: https://drive.redwood.ai/share/1FablePay-p95-dump

Apologies again for the impact during your promo window — we appreciate the early report which helped accelerate our rollback. Please let us know if you want a separate call; otherwise we’ll send the postmortem by EOD tomorrow.

Thanks —
Jasmine Liu
Customer Reliability Manager, Redwood Inference
